evidence: The structural core exists and works: src/Forge.App/MauiProgram.cs:20-110 boots DevExpress in the correct order behind a themed shell; src/Forge.App/Hosting/AppShell.xaml:27-38 renders five tab destinations; src/Forge.App/Features/FeatureRegistration.cs:47-74 composes 22 self-registering feature modules; src/Forge.Core/Abstractions/INavigationService.cs is a MAUI-free navigation abstraction with 46 route constants in src/Forge.App/Navigation/ForgeRoutes.cs. F01.01 and F01.02 are largely delivered.
gaps: F01.03 is almost entirely absent: there is no src/Forge.Infrastructure/Diagnostics directory, no file log sink, no rotation, no redaction policy, no global exception handler, no recovery screen and no OnSleep/OnResume state persistence. Grep for 'GlobalExceptionHandler|UnhandledException|UnobservedTaskException|RecoveryPage|FileLoggerProvider|ForgeLogEvents' over src/ returns zero matches. The epic outcome sentence 'logs structurally ... survives suspend and resume with state intact, and fails gracefully with a recoverable error surface rather than a crash' is unmet on all three counts.

evidence: Forge.slnx declares four src projects and three test projects; src/Directory.Build.targets:14-34 implements the compiler-enforced architecture guard (FORGE001/FORGE002) and tests/Forge.Core.Tests/Architecture/DependencyRuleTests.cs:33-51 backs it at the assembly level. Directory.Packages.props is the only version source - no PackageReference in src/ or tests/ carries an inline Version attribute. src/Forge.App/MauiProgram.cs:35-70 sets ThemeManager before CreateBuilder and chains all six DevExpress registrations after UseMauiApp. src/Forge.App/Features/FeatureRegistration.cs is the single delimited registration list.
gaps: The Forge.Health project required by S01.01.01 does not exist; health code lives in src/Forge.App/Services/Health instead. No Forge.App test project exists, so no ViewModel or shell behaviour is covered by any test.

evidence: Forge.slnx lists src/Forge.App, src/Forge.Core, src/Forge.Domain, src/Forge.Infrastructure and tests/Forge.Core.Tests, tests/Forge.Domain.Tests, tests/Forge.Infrastructure.Tests. src/Forge.App/Forge.App.csproj:20-21 sets TargetFrameworks to net10.0-android plus net10.0-ios (the latter conditioned off on Linux with an in-file explanation about NETSDK1178); no Windows or Mac Catalyst TFM appears anywhere. Lines 42-43 set SupportedOSPlatformVersion 26.0 for Android and 15.0 for iOS, meeting the minimum-SDK requirement. src/Directory.Build.targets:27-33 raises MSBuild errors FORGE001 (forbidden Microsoft.Maui*/DevExpress* PackageReference) and FORGE002 (inverted ProjectReference) for Forge.Domain and Forge.Core, satisfying AC2. A repository-wide scan of src/*/*.csproj and tests/*/*.csproj found no PackageReference with an inline Version attribute, so all versions resolve from Directory.Packages.props.
gaps: REQ1 unmet: there is no Forge.Health project under src/ and no Forge.Health.Tests under tests/. Health code sits in src/Forge.App/Services/Health and src/Forge.Core/Abstractions/Health, so the layer the requirement names as a separate assembly was never created. Also, there is no Forge.App test project, so 'matching unit test projects' holds for three of the four assemblies that do exist. AC1 ('zero warnings') and AC2/AC3 as build outcomes were not executed - this is a read-only verification and a full multi-TFM build was out of scope; note that Directory.Build.props only sets TreatWarningsAsErrors when ContinuousIntegrationBuild is true, so a local zero-warning build is not enforced. AC3's literal wording ('exactly net10.0-android and net10.0-ios') is satisfied on Windows and macOS but not on Linux, where the conditional drops iOS.

evidence: src/Forge.App/MauiProgram.cs:35-36 assigns ThemeManager.UseAndroidSystemColor = false and ThemeManager.Theme = new Theme(Color.FromArgb(ForgeBrand.SeedHex)) as the first non-instrumentation statements in CreateMauiApp, before MauiApp.CreateBuilder() on line 40, exactly as the requirement demands. Lines 50-70 chain .UseMauiApp(...) followed by .UseDevExpress(useLocalization: false), .UseDevExpressControls(), .UseDevExpressCollectionView(), .UseDevExpressEditors(), .UseDevExpressCharts() and .UseDevExpressGauges() - all six required suites, all after UseMauiApp, in a single chained expression so analyzer DXM001 sees the syntactic relationship it checks (the in-file comment on lines 44-49 records why the chain must not be split). src/Forge.App/Branding/ForgeBrand.cs supplies the seed colour, and src/Forge.App/Hosting/AppShell.xaml:20-24 consumes the derived palette through dx:ThemeColor roles rather than hex literals.

The convention is real and universally applied: src/Forge.App/Features/FeatureRegistration.cs:47-74 calls 22 Add<Name>Feature extension methods in one alphabetical block, and MauiProgram.cs:95-97 reduces the shared surface to three lines (AddForgeInfrastructure, AddForgeShell, AddForgeFeatures). Each feature owns its registration file - e.g. src/Forge.App/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingFeatureRegistration.cs:24-63 registers its pages and view models transient (lines 28-31), its stores singleton (line 32), and registers its own routes (lines 59-60). src/Forge.App/Composition/InfrastructureRegistration.cs:46-50 registers ForgeDbContext transient with a documented rationale, and lines 57-61 register IDataSessionFactory singleton, satisfying the DbContext-lifetime requirement.
gaps: AC1's 'the only conflicting line is within the delimited registration block' is undermined by a live counter-example: AppShell is bound twice - src/Forge.App/MauiProgram.cs:124 (services.AddSingleton<AppShell>()) and src/Forge.App/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingFeatureRegistration.cs:34-57 (a factory that attaches FirstRunGate to shell.Loaded). Because AddForgeFeatures runs after AddForgeShell, the Onboarding binding silently wins. This is the same failure shape as the IDataErasureService double-binding: correctness depends on registration order rather than being stated, and a second feature registering AppShell would silently displace first-run routing with no build or test failure. AC2 ('all dependencies resolve without a runtime resolution exception') cannot be grounded by reading - it needs a container validation pass or a device launch, and there is no Forge.App test project that would catch it.

evidence: src/Forge.App/Hosting/AppShell.xaml:27-38 declares a five-destination TabBar; src/Forge.Core/Abstractions/INavigationService.cs declares GoToAsync/GoBackAsync/ShowModalAsync with no MAUI types; src/Forge.App/Navigation/ForgeRoutes.cs holds 46 route constants and 21 feature registration files call Routing.RegisterRoute against them, so call sites use constants rather than magic strings.
gaps: The feature outcome promises 'correct hardware back behaviour on Android' for modal flows. ShowModalAsync is dead code (no caller in src/) and its //route implementation cannot work for a globally registered route; nothing intercepts hardware back; nothing restores scroll position. Tabs carry no icons, so tab selection is conveyed by colour alone.

evidence: src/Forge.App/Hosting/AppShell.xaml:27-38 declares exactly the five required destinations - Today, Train, Nutrition, Progress, Profile - each with a Route matching a ForgeRoutes constant and a ContentTemplate pointing at a real page type. Lines 20-24 style the tab bar from DevExpress semantic roles (SurfaceContainer, Primary, OnSurfaceVariant), so light/dark follows the theme rather than hex literals. src/Forge.App/Hosting/AppShell.xaml.cs:7-11 sets BindingContext from the injected AppShellViewModel.
gaps: REQ1 unmet as written: navigation uses MAUI Shell's TabBar, not dx:TabView. The XAML comment on lines 14-18 argues Shell owns routing and back stack while TabView is a content control - a defensible call - but docs/architecture/overview.md:79 still states 'Primary navigation | dx:TabView', so the codebase contradicts its own architecture document and no ADR records the change. REQ2/AC1 unmet: no ShellContent carries an Icon, so tab selection is signalled by colour alone (TabBarTitleColor vs TabBarUnselectedColor). That fails WCAG 1.4.1 and directly contradicts AC1's 'conveyed by both an icon change and a colour change'. REQ3/AC2 unmet: nothing persists or restores the selected tab. AppShellViewModel.SelectedTabIndex (src/Forge.App/Hosting/AppShellViewModel.cs:17-18) is declared and documented as 'Persisted on suspend' but is never read or written anywhere in src/, and AppShell.xaml binds nothing to it - it is write-only-never-even-written state. App.xaml.cs has no OnSleep or OnResume override. A process kill always returns the user to Today. AC3 (screen-reader announcement) is only partly grounded: no SemanticProperties are set on any ShellContent, so announcements depend entirely on the platform reading Title; selected-state announcement is not asserted anywhere. AC4 (gesture-navigation safe area) cannot be judged by reading and needs a device.

evidence: src/Forge.Core/Abstractions/INavigationService.cs:11-31 declares the interface in Forge.Core with exactly GoToAsync, GoBackAsync and ShowModalAsync, taking object? for the parameter so no dictionary appears at the call site. tests/Forge.Core.Tests/Architecture/DependencyRuleTests.cs:54-68 asserts no framework namespace leaks into any INavigationService signature, which grounds the substitutability requirement. src/Forge.App/Navigation/ForgeRoutes.cs declares all 46 destinations as constants and every Routing.RegisterRoute call across 21 feature registration files uses those constants. src/Forge.App/Navigation/ShellNavigationService.cs:36-54 marshals the typed parameter into Shell's dictionary under a single private key and throws a descriptive InvalidOperationException when Shell.Current is null.
gaps: AC1 unmet in practice: no ViewModel test with a substituted INavigationService exists anywhere - there is no Forge.App test project, and grep for INavigationService across tests/ matches only DependencyRuleTests. The abstraction is testable; nothing tests through it. AC2 unmet: ShellNavigationService performs no route validation at all - it forwards straight to Shell.GoToAsync, so the exception a caller sees is whatever MAUI raises, not a Forge exception that names the offending route, and no test pins the message. AC3 unmet and structurally broken: ShowModalAsync (line 26-27) prefixes the route with '//', which in MAUI Shell means an absolute route that resets the navigation stack to a Shell item - but every non-tab destination in Forge is a global route registered with Routing.RegisterRoute, and MAUI refuses an absolute navigation whose only page is a global route. Worse, ShowModalAsync has no caller anywhere in src/ (grep finds only the interface declaration and the implementation); pages that need modal presentation instead set Shell.TabBarIsVisible="False" on themselves - e.g. src/Forge.App/Features/Workout/ActiveWorkoutPage.xaml:10 - and are reached with ordinary GoToAsync. Nothing intercepts the Android hardware back button and nothing preserves the underlying tab's scroll position.

evidence: Grep over src/ for 'GlobalExceptionHandler|UnhandledException|UnobservedTaskException|RecoveryPage|FileLoggerProvider|ForgeLogEvents' returns zero matches. src/Forge.Infrastructure has no Diagnostics directory (its only folders are Backup, Content, Media and Persistence). The only logging configuration in the app is src/Forge.App/MauiProgram.cs:101-103, a DEBUG-only builder.Logging.AddDebug(). The only failure surface is src/Forge.App/App.xaml.cs:57-62, which writes a startup fault to Debug.WriteLine and its own comment defers the user-facing surface to 'the recovery surface (E01/F01.03)' - which does not exist.
gaps: None of the three stories in this feature is delivered. There is no file log sink, no rotation, no redaction rule, no exception boundary, no recovery screen, no diagnostic-sharing consent flow and no suspend/resume state snapshot. The feature outcome - 'a crash-free-feeling app where unexpected failures produce a recoverable screen and a local diagnostic record the user can choose to share' - has no implementation behind it.

evidence: The implementation notes point at src/Forge.Infrastructure/Diagnostics/FileLoggerProvider.cs and ForgeLogEvents.cs. Neither file exists; src/Forge.Infrastructure contains only Backup/, Content/, Media/ and Persistence/. Grep over src/ for ILoggerProvider or AddLogging returns no provider registration of any kind. The complete logging configuration is src/Forge.App/MauiProgram.cs:101-103: '#if DEBUG builder.Logging.AddDebug(); #endif'. Structured source-generated logging is used correctly where it is used - src/Forge.App/Composition/ForgeStartup.cs:177-187 declares four [LoggerMessage] events - but in a Release build those events go nowhere because no provider is registered.
gaps: Every requirement is unmet. No file sink writes to the app cache directory (REQ1). No rotation at 5 MB and no three-file retention exists anywhere (REQ2, AC2). No redaction rule or policy prevents bodyweight, heart rate, food names or free-text notes from being logged - there is no allow-list, no scrubber and no test asserting their absence (REQ3, AC1). Release builds have no sink at all, so REQ5's 'Debug builds additionally log to the platform debug console' is inverted: Debug is the only build that logs. AC3 (no frame exceeding 16.6 ms attributable to logging) cannot be judged by reading and would need on-device frame timing; it is moot while no sink exists.

evidence: The implementation notes point at src/Forge.App/Diagnostics/GlobalExceptionHandler.cs and src/Forge.App/Features/Diagnostics/RecoveryPage.xaml. Neither file nor either directory exists - src/Forge.App has no Diagnostics folder and Features/ has no Diagnostics subfolder. Grep over src/ for UnhandledException, UnobservedTaskException, AppDomain.CurrentDomain or TaskScheduler returns no handler registration. ForgeRoutes.cs declares no recovery route, so there is nothing to navigate to. The closest thing to a failure surface is src/Forge.App/App.xaml.cs:53-63, which swallows a startup failure into System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine and explicitly defers user presentation to this story.
gaps: All five requirements are unmet. Nothing captures UI-thread unhandled exceptions or unobserved task exceptions, so an unhandled exception terminates the process (AC1 unmet). There is no recovery screen and therefore no Continue, Restart or Share diagnostics affordance (AC2, AC3 unmet). There is no diagnostic payload, no preview-before-share confirmation and no transmission path - the last of which means REQ5 ('no automatic transmission') is trivially true but for the wrong reason. Note the interaction with the workout flush requirement: src/Forge.App/Features/Workout/WorkoutPersistenceService.cs does commit sets to the database as they are logged, so in-progress work would survive a crash, but that is incidental to this story rather than the flush-on-boundary it specifies.

evidence: The in-progress-workout half of this story is genuinely delivered, though by a different mechanism than specified: src/Forge.App/Features/Workout/WorkoutPersistenceService.cs:166-260 writes ActiveWorkoutState and each logged set to the encrypted database as they happen, and lines 146-163 reload the state on next launch, classifying it with Forge.Domain.Workout.WorkoutRecoveryPolicy.Classify. src/Forge.Domain/Workout/WorkoutRecoveryPolicy.cs:8 sets DefaultStaleAfter = TimeSpan.FromHours(12), matching the story's 12-hour rule, and src/Forge.App/Features/Workout/ActiveWorkoutPageViewModel.cs:792-798 surfaces Resume and Stale outcomes to the user. So AC1 - three logged sets present after a process kill - is satisfied by continuous write-through rather than by an OnSleep snapshot.
gaps: The navigation half is entirely missing. src/Forge.App/App.xaml.cs overrides only CreateWindow and OnStart - there is no OnSleep or OnResume override anywhere in src/, so nothing persists on suspend as REQ1 requires. The named artefact src/Forge.App/Shell/AppStateSnapshot.cs does not exist. Selected tab and active route are never captured: AppShellViewModel.SelectedTabIndex (src/Forge.App/Hosting/AppShellViewModel.cs:17-18) is declared with the comment 'Persisted on suspend' and is neither read nor written by any other file, and AppShell.xaml binds nothing to it. AC2 is only accidentally satisfied - the app always opens on Today because no tab is ever restored, not because stale state is discarded; and the 13-hour workout case shows a 'finish it now or discard it' prompt rather than being discarded silently. Separately, src/Forge.App/Features/Workout/ActiveWorkoutDraftStore.cs implements a Preferences-backed draft store and is registered at WorkoutFeatureRegistration.cs:30, but no type injects IActiveWorkoutDraftStore - it is registered dead code, and it applies no staleness rule of its own. AC3 (restoration adding no more than 100 ms to cold start) cannot be judged by reading, and is moot while restoration does not exist.
